chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ibn al-Mughirah, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father عليه السلام, who said:
The one performing tayammum must not lead in prayer those who have wudu (ablution), and the one afflicted with paralysis must not lead the healthy.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمِ: tayammum, dry ablution used in place of wudu under specific conditions
key_terms.يَؤُمُّ: leads as Imam in congregational salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Can a person with tayammum lead people with wudu in congregational prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about who may lead congregational salat (prayer). It states that a person praying with tayammum should not lead those with wudu (ablution), and that a person afflicted with paralysis should not lead those who are physically sound.
